EXPLANATION: The strong low-frequency band at 673 cm⁻¹ points to a halogen-related stretch; among the candidates, only O=C1OCCN1SCl contains a Cl atom and an S–Cl bond, which commonly gives Raman bands in the 650–700 cm⁻¹ region. The carbonyl at 1778 cm⁻¹ is consistent with a strained cyclic carbamate/lactone-type C=O. Additional bands near 760–820 cm⁻¹ and ~952 cm⁻¹ are plausible for N–S/Cl-related modes and ring vibrations in this heterocycle. Aliphatic C–H stretches at 2895/2974 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003) and CH bending near 1437 cm⁻¹ further fit this structure, whereas other candidates lack halogens to account for the intense 673 cm⁻¹ feature.
